title: Linux_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_942
description: Investigate and respond to a Linux/Remaiten botnet infection, focusing on identifying suspicious services, command-and-control communication, and flood attack targets.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these issues. The Linux/Remaiten botnet is known for its periodic beaconing to command-and-control servers and its ability to launch flood attacks against targeted systems.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external host?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is named 'bot-beacon.service'.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Start by understanding the types of services that might be running on a Linux system and how they can be malicious.

hints.title: Command Suggestion
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all running services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a service named 'bot-beacon.service' in the list of running services.

levels.title: Determine Command-and-Control Server
levels.content:
Determine the external host communicating with the compromised system.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the command-and-control server?
levels.solution: Investigate network connections and logs for external communication. The command-and-control server is at IP address 192.168.70.5.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Understand that command-and-control servers typically communicate with compromised systems over the network.

hints.title: Command Suggestion
hints.content: Use the command 'ss -tulnp' to list all network connections.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a connection to the IP address 192.168.70.5 in the network connections.

levels.title: Identify Flood Attack Target
levels.content:
Identify the system receiving the abnormal volume of network traffic generated by the compromised host.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the system being targeted by the flood attack?
levels.solution: Analyze network traffic to identify the victim of the flooding activity. The target system is at IP address 192.168.80.100.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Flood attacks typically involve sending a large volume of network traffic to a target system.

hints.title: Command Suggestion
hints.content: Use the command 'tcpdump -i any' to capture and analyze network traffic.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a high volume of traffic being sent to the IP address 192.168.80.100 in the network traffic.
